listening.title: A call with a supplier about the delivery date

lines.speaker: Hoa (Procurement Officer)
lines.text: Good morning, this is Hoa from VietSoft. Is Mr Duc on the line?

lines.speaker: Duc (Partner Account Manager)
lines.text: Speaking. Good morning, Hoa. Thank you for calling. How can I help today?

lines.speaker: Hoa (Procurement Officer)
lines.text: I have two points about the delivery schedule. May I start with the first?

lines.speaker: Duc (Partner Account Manager)
lines.text: Please go ahead. I have my notes open and about fifteen free minutes.

lines.speaker: Hoa (Procurement Officer)
lines.text: Our team needs the new licences before Friday. Is that date still possible?

lines.speaker: Duc (Partner Account Manager)
lines.text: It is tight, but yes. I will send written confirmation this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Hoa (Procurement Officer)
lines.text: Thank you. Please use my work email, not the general company address.

lines.speaker: Duc (Partner Account Manager)
lines.text: Could you spell it out slowly? I want to avoid sending it to the wrong inbox.

lines.speaker: Hoa (Procurement Officer)
lines.text: Of course: H-O-A, then vietsoft dot vn. Shall I recap the call quickly?

lines.speaker: Duc (Partner Account Manager)
lines.text: Yes please, that always helps both of us remember the agreed points.

lines.speaker: Hoa (Procurement Officer)
lines.text: You confirm the licences by Friday and email me the signed delivery schedule.

lines.speaker: Duc (Partner Account Manager)
lines.text: Correct. If I am out, my assistant will take a message and I will call back later.

options: To ask about the delivery schedule
To apply for a new position
To complain about a broken laptop

questions.q: What will Duc send this afternoon?
Why does Duc ask Hoa to spell her email?
options: He wants to avoid the wrong inbox
He has no computer with him
